result.title: Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning
result.comment: Published at NeurIPS 2026. 53 pages, 19 figures, 6 tables
result.summary: Large language models can have behaviours which only arise in hard-to-anticipate contexts. These hidden behaviours pose a challenge to alignment audits, which seek to uncover problematic model behaviour but are limited by the scenarios the auditor can anticipate. To address this challenge, we explore limited-parameter finetuning (LPF) on examples of a target behaviour. While training 3-25% of LoRA parameters, LPF reveals whether the model has a hidden behaviour, even when standard behavioural evaluations cannot. LPF succeeds on a suite of model organisms with hidden behaviours (8-14B parameters), and also surfaces naturally occurring hidden behaviours in open-weight models (27-35B parameters). LPF can thus distinguish between models which appear behaviourally identical to an auditor, and does not require the context in which the hidden behaviour surfaces. LPF provides a novel affordance that may be useful for auditing frontier AI models. However, we do not evaluate LPF against baselines in a realistic auditing setting, so further work is needed to determine its practicality.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出有限参数微调（LPF）：仅训练 3–25% 的 LoRA 参数，用少量目标行为样例检验模型是否潜藏该行为，并在 8–35B 的模型生物与开源权重模型上借此区分表面行为相同的模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用轻量适配探测内部是否留存未被表现出的能力」的审计思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节是否仍存在于内部状态、以及 latent 内容是否被答案实际使用这类表示与因果作用问题。
